prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a smooth brightness gradient along the two-lane paved road directly in front of and below the camera wearer, ranging from about 1.5–2 metres at the bottom edge to over 30 metres toward the vanishing point, flanked by a gravel median with double-headed lampposts on the left and a raised curb, sidewalk, palm trees, and buildings on the right. Across the five frames, the camera wearer moves rapidly forward along the road while the camera rolls counter-clockwise (tilting left), causing roadside structures to approach and pass out of view on the left and right edges: a right-side lamppost and palm tree approach from roughly 6–8 metres in frame 1 to 2–3 metres in frame 2 before exiting right, while a left-side median lamppost approaches from over 15 metres in frame 1 to roughly 3–4 metres on the far left by frame 5. No people or objects are within arm's reach (~1 metre) of the camera wearer at any point, and the palm trees and lampposts partially occlude the white building facades ~10–15 metres to the right and the opposite roadway ~8–15 metres to the left. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clearly isolates the foreground vertical silhouettes and relative distances of the thin lamppost poles, curb edges, and palm trunks against the cluttered background, though it is unreliable on fine palm fronds where background sky bleeds through and in the far distance beyond ~25 metres where structures merge into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is completely black across all five frames, detecting zero object or person instances in the scene. In the RGB context, the environment contains static roadside infrastructure—paved road lanes, curbs, a gravel median, metal lampposts, palm trees, white buildings on the right (~10–20 metres away), and small trash bins on the right sidewalk (~8–15 metres away in frames 1–3)—along with tiny, distant figures or posts barely visible on the far-left sidewalk over 25–30 metres away. Because no masks are rendered, the segmentation map provides no spatial layout, relative positions, occlusion boundaries, or frame-to-frame motion tracking on its own, though the absence of detections is consistent with the lack of any people, vehicles, or manipulable objects within arm's reach or in the near-to-mid foreground (1–10 metres). The map is unreliable for understanding scene structure because it fails to segment the road, sidewalk, lampposts, trash bins, or any distant background objects visible in the RGB frames.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand pose map is entirely black across all five frames, containing no yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons. Using the RGB strip for context, the camera wearer's own body and hands are completely out of the field of view below the camera frustum, and there are no nearby people in front, to the left, or to the right on the road or adjacent sidewalks as the camera wearer travels forward. Consequently, no person's facing direction, gaze toward the camera wearer, interpersonal distance, or reach space can be established, and nothing is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or any detected person across the sequence. While the empty pose map accurately reflects the absence of foreground pedestrians in the immediate 1–15 metre range, it provides no spatial information beyond the RGB image and cannot capture any tiny, distant figures over 25–30 metres away on the far-left walkway.
